newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares slide to end electronic trade lower.
newsitem.headline: German shares slide to end electronic trade lower.

text.p: German shares plunged in afternoon electronic trade on Wednesday, after jittery markets reacted sharply to an unwelcome fall on Wall Street and surrendered ground gained in bourse trade.

Shares fell after a lower opening on the Dow Jones Industrial index on Wall Street and the IBIS DAX index of 30 blue-chip German shares ended the day down 2.15 percent, 70.52 points, at 3,210.94 points.

This was one of the sharpest falls in the index since November and meant the index more than lost the ground it made up in bourse trade, when the DAX index ended up 5.98 points, or up 0.18 percent, at 3,301.91 points.
"This market is paranoid and nervous about everything and is responding dramatically to every sort of pressure. It is also a very technical market," said one equities trader.

The Dow Jones Industrial index was down over half a percent at 6,574.79 points in late German trade, driving German shares further down and conclusively penetrating the 3,300 point support threshold mentioned earlier by dealers.
Losses were spread pretty much across the board. The major sectors, such as the banks and the chemical companies, experienced heavy losses.

Deutsche Bank AG ended down 1.48 marks, 1.64 percent, at 88.60 marks, while Dresdner Bank AG ended the day down 13 pfennigs, or 0.22 percent, at 44.71 marks and Commerzbank ended down 1.39 marks, or three percent, at 44.71 marks.
Early gainers, including chemical giant BASF AG, which climbed after giving an upbeat outlook for the current business year, were also hit by the slide.

BASF ended down 96 pfennigs, or 1.58 percent, at 59.69 marks. Other chemical stocks also fell at the last, including Bayer, down 1.24 marks, or 1.83 percent, at 66.40 marks, and Hoechst, down 1.20 marks, or 1.86 percent, at 63.20 marks.
